approved: Australian Border Force Amendment (Protected Information) Bill 2017
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would narrow the definition of protected information in the Australian Border Force Act 2015 to cover only specific kinds of information.
It would remove the current requirement for disclosure rules to be prescribed in a legislative instrument, which the government says is ineffective and reduces efficiency.

The bill would add three new permitted purposes for disclosing protected information that contains personal information: inter-country adoption, national security and defence of Australia, and locating missing persons.
Repeal the broad definition of protected information and replace it with a definition of Immigration and Border Protection information.
Remove paragraphs 44(2)(d) and 45(2)(d) of the Australian Border Force Act 2015.
Add three new permitted purposes for disclosing personal information under the Act.
The Department of Immigration and Border Protection, including the Australian Border Force, and entrusted persons who handle information.

Australian Border Force Amendment (Protected Information) Bill 2017 - in Committee - Unauthorised disclosure

The Australian Border Force Amendment (Protected Information) Bill 2017 was moved to clarify and refine secrecy and disclosure provisions in the Australian Border Force Act 2015, ensuring sensitive information is protected while allowing appropriate disclosures for legitimate purposes; the bill applies retrospectively to the original enactment date.

Labor supported the bill to narrow the definition of protected information, but argued the minister, not the department secretary, should have the power to prescribe additional protected information; it also criticised the government for failing to act on the Senate inquiry’s recommendations regarding offshore processing centres.

The Australian Border Force Amendment (Protected Information) Bill 2017 was supported for narrowing the definition of protected information and enabling offshore detention staff to speak more freely; the government was criticised for indefinite detention on Manus Island and Nauru, and for cutting income and accommodation support to 370 asylum seekers brought to Australia for medical treatment.

The speaker supported the Australian Border Force Amendment (Protected Information) Bill 2017 but called for further amendments to ensure ministerial rather than departmental control, and urged greater transparency and compassion in asylum seeker policies, citing concerns from constituents and organisations including Save the Children and Rural Australians for Refugees.

The speaker supported the Australian Border Force Amendment (Protected Information) Bill 2017, arguing it narrows protected information provisions to focus on immigration and border protection while allowing public accountability for government conduct, and noted the US resettlement deal to reduce detention time on Manus Island and Nauru.

The Australian Border Force Amendment (Protected Information) Bill 2017 was commended to the House, clarifying secrecy provisions with retrospective effect to narrow protected information to categories posing identifiable harm, while retaining two-year penalties for unauthorised disclosure by entrusted persons. The speech also cited the government's national security reforms, including a new Office of National Intelligence, a home affairs portfolio, and nearly $60 million for biometric technology and almost $100 million for visa risk assessment.

The Australian Border Force Amendment (Protected Information) Bill 2017 clarifies part 6 of the Australian Border Force Act to prevent unauthorised disclosure of information harmful to national or public interest, while allowing appropriate disclosure, with retrospective application to 2015.

The government moved amendments to the Australian Border Force Amendment (Protected Information) Bill 2017 to replace the secretary with the minister as the authority to prescribe additional kinds of "immigration and border protection information" by legislative instrument, addressing concerns about an unelected official exercising this power.
